channel.title: cursivee.app blog
channel.description: Practical guides to cursive text and other fancy Unicode text: names, bios, the cursive alphabet, fonts and how it all works.

item.title: How to write your name in cursive
item.description: Type your name once and copy it in cursive: which style suits the letters your name has, popular names already converted, and where a cursive name will and won't paste.

item.title: Cursive bio ideas to copy and paste
item.description: Forty-eight short bio lines already in cursive — aesthetic, minimal, funny, love and birthday — plus the layout rules that keep a cursive bio readable.

item.title: Cursive fonts in Google Docs, Word and Canva
item.description: Documents have real font menus. Where to find cursive fonts in Google Docs, Word and Canva, which ones read well, and when to use a generator instead.

item.title: How a cursive generator actually works
item.description: A cursive generator never touches your font. The Unicode block behind it, the eleven missing letters, and why cursive text counts double and hides from search.

item.title: How to put cursive text in your Instagram bio
item.description: Instagram has no font setting, yet cursive bios exist. Here is how they work, where they paste cleanly on Instagram, TikTok, Discord and X, and where they fail.

item.title: The cursive alphabet, A to Z, to copy and paste
item.description: Every cursive letter A to Z in script, bold script and Old English, ready to copy and paste, plus the eleven letters that behave differently and why.

item.title: Why fancy text shows up as boxes or question marks
item.description: Empty boxes, question marks or plain letters where your fancy text should be? Each has a different cause. Here is how to tell them apart and fix each one.

item.title: Can screen readers read fancy text?
item.description: Mostly no. Screen readers announce cursive Unicode as maths symbols or skip it entirely. What that sounds like, who else it affects, and how to use it well.

item.title: What is Zalgo text, and how does it work?
item.description: Zalgo or glitch text is ordinary letters buried under stacked accent marks. How it works, where the name came from, why apps differ, and how to remove it.
